claims.statement: Aria2RpcServer::serve refuses to start when the configured listen_address is non-loopback and authentication is disabled, then assembles a Router with POST and GET /jsonrpc (HTTP and WebSocket), applies the CORS layer captured by new(), and runs axum gracefully shut down by a watch receiver; on loopback with AuthConfig::Disabled it starts but logs a warning naming the address.
bind_with_retry retries AddrInUse for a 5-second window at 25 ms intervals to survive the settings hot-reload handoff, while any other bind error is returned immediately.
AuthConfig has three states — Disabled, Shared{secret} and PerClient — and per-client mode with an empty client list fails closed rather than degrading to anonymous access.

check_token accepts only a token:-prefixed first parameter, uses constant-time comparison for the shared secret and Argon2 verification for per-client tokens; dispatch_method calls it for every routed method except the anonymous system.listMethods/listNotifications and the outer multicall call.

dispatch_method enforces the token centrally before strip_token and then routes via dispatch_authorized, which is deliberate because per-handler checks were previously inverted and some bulk methods skipped authentication; system.listMethods/listNotifications, and the outer multicall call, are anonymous, while every nested multicall is authenticated individually by routing back through dispatch_method.

Tokens are 32 random bytes URL-safe base64, persisted only as an Argon2id PHC hash; verification is constant-time, malformed hashes are a non-match, and successful verifications are cached in memory by BLAKE3 digest and never persisted.

A GID is xxh3_64 of the internal task id formatted as 16 hex digits; resolve_gid checks the cache then scans every backend's list(), resolving an exact match or a unique prefix (an ambiguous prefix is refused), and caches only full GIDs.
remove, removeDownloadResult and purgeDownloadResult evict their GID cache entries, preventing unbounded cache growth in long sessions.

dispatch_authorized maps the implemented aria2 methods and system.listMethods advertises exactly that set — 36 entries including getServers, changeUri, changePosition and forceShutdown; addMetalink is the only aria2 method intentionally absent, and the Tier 1 contract test asserts both the equality and that every advertised method is reachable (recognized by its error message, since every domain error is code 1).

system.multicall dispatches each nested call through dispatch_method (so it is authenticated on its own) and wraps each result in a single-element array ([value] or [{"code","message"}]) because AriaNg/Motrix read element 0.
classify_aria2_uri routes only magnet: URIs to BT; an http(s) .torrent URL stays HTTP because aria2 downloads it as a plain file and uses addTorrent for the parsed form.

addUri treats the uris array as an ordered candidate list (element 0 primary, rest as HTTP mirrors), reads the optional trailing options/position by JSON type rather than position, translates header/referer/http-user/checksum/user-agent/split/max-tries/out/dir/pause options, maps a position of 0 to High priority, and deduplicates a non-terminal HTTP task by returning its existing GID.

changeOption supports only pause, select-file (1-based BT indices) and max-download-limit/max-upload-limit (BT), errors with the key name for any other option, and preserves the untouched direction when setting one BT limit.
summary_for_raw_id falls back to the database download header for tasks evicted from memory, keeping terminal results queryable until purgeDownloadResult or removeDownloadResult.

The keys filter is supported with aria2's positional indices — 1 for tellStatus, 0 for tellActive, 2 for tellWaiting and tellStopped — and tellStopped also reads list_download_headers and count_terminal_downloads.

HTTP lifecycle notifications are broadcast by the RPC handler only when the task kind is Http, while all BT aria2 notifications come exclusively from the BT alert bridge, preventing duplicate notifications.

RpcContext::http() and RpcContext::bt() are the only sanctioned protocol-specific get_typed downcasts in the aria2 layer, and the RPC surface is inherently protocol-specific so those accesses are centralized there.

Aria2RpcSettings::default() has enabled = false because an empty secret yields AuthConfig::Disabled (anonymous loopback RPC); enabling the service is an explicit user action and an existing settings.json with "enabled": true is honoured. AuthConfig::is_enabled is pub(crate) so serve can check it before the context moves into the router.

summary_to_aria2_status emits aria2’s always-present status keys plus BT top-level infoHash/numSeeders/seeder and terminal-only errorCode/errorMessage (0 for no error, 1 for failure), while enrich_status adds HTTP bitfield/numPieces/pieceLength from the live manifest chunk map and the BT bittorrent object (mode/info.name/announceList) plus BT bitfield/numPieces.

getServers reports one server per URI candidate (or BT trackers), changeUri removes/inserts URIs through DownloadManager::change_task_uris and returns [deleted, added] while refusing to empty the list, changePosition maps the requested index onto the three priority levels and returns the actual resulting index from the shared waiting order, and forceShutdown aliases the shutdown handler.

Trailing RPC arguments are parsed by JSON type via split_aria2_tail so both AriaNg’s addTorrent([torrent, [], options]) and the legacy [torrent, options] shape keep dir/out/pause/select-file, and the Tier 1 interop suite encodes those real client shapes as a regression guard.

aria2_rpc/oracle_tests.rs is a Tier 2 live-aria2c oracle (opt-in via ARIA2_ORACLE_BIN, nightly/manual Linux workflow) that asserts the client-facing contract against allowlists — AriaNg option keys, always-present tellStatus keys, the listMethods/listNotifications delta, code 1 error objects and JSON-RPC batch — and fails on anything outside them.

aria2.getVersion reports the real CARGO_PKG_VERSION and a truthful enabledFeatures list (Async DNS, BitTorrent, GZip, Brotli, Zstd, HTTPS, Message Digest), omitting Metalink/SFTP/XML-RPC/Firefox3 Cookie; the Tier 1 test interop_get_version_is_truthful locks it.
is_loopback_bind_address treats 127.0.0.1, ::1 and the localhost hostname as loopback and everything that does not parse as an IP as public, so the bind gate fails closed for an unrecognized host.
format_bind_addr brackets an IPv6 literal so ::1 is rendered as [::1]:<port> instead of the malformed ::1:<port>.

build_cors_layer emits Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and omits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials when allow_any_origin is set, echoes configured origins otherwise, and falls back to localhost with a warning when every configured origin fails to parse.

aria2.shutdown publishes a warning and acknowledges in all modes but calls RpcContext::shutdown_notify.notify_one() only when exit_on_shutdown is set; the desktop leaves it false and the headless daemon sets it true.
Domain failures (unknown method, invalid params, unknown GID, unauthorized, internal) answer aria2's code: 1; only wire-level parse and version failures keep -32700/-32600.

A POST or WebSocket body may be a top-level JSON-RPC 2.0 batch; each element is dispatched, notifications execute without a response entry, an all-notification batch returns no body, and an empty array is a single Invalid Request.

getGlobalOption and getOption answer AriaNg's complete global and task option key sets (pinned by Tier 1 and the Tier 2 oracle), using real limedl settings where an equivalent exists and aria2 defaults otherwise; changeGlobalOption applies the mappable subset and ignores unrecognized keys.
